quest.title: The Recollector's Path
quest.description: After completing some of the training assignments recommended by Zurvan, Sorush grows closer to assuming the responsibilities of a Bloomguard...\n
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x10, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: It appears the first part of your training went well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah. Maybe it was a bit too easy for Sorush?

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Ha. Then I look forward to seeing her coming performance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right. About listening to Sorush tell stories, it turned out that Sorush went through a rebellious phase—

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Speak no more of this!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Ahem. Anyhow, I have finally sh—shed that stage of my life.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: The important thing is that I, with my Yasnapati and the Pale Floater, recalled the history following the birth of the Pari, and spoke of the familiars of the forest and their special festival.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: The fact that we, as Pari, do not have such a celebration of our own makes me troubled. Do you not feel the same way, Elder?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: If it were up to me, we should let humans attend the Pari Festival, and hear from them the praises they sing for the Pari. Afterward, I shall pick the best singer...

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: To my knowledge, Festival Utsava is not a day to be so willfully and wastefully spent.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Uh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon always thought Sorush's desire to get humans to record her deeds was different from the other Pari... Is this also the influence of the Order of Skeptics?

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: That is the very reason why recalling and pondering the past is significant.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Ha. Whatever happens, I look forward to seeing her coming performance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sorush isn't nearly as amazing as she says she is, so she'll have to try even harder for what comes next.

talks.objective: Head to the specified location and complete the trial
Head to the specified location and complete the trial

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait! Paimon remembers this place? We've been here before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It sure scared Paimon pretty good!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon remembers that Sorush said this Wenut got sealed here because it was unlucky. Though, what does it have to do with Sorush's training?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh. Does Zurvan actually mean to say: "Haha. Behold, Sorush! Behold the fate of the unfortunate"?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hm... My elder is no Pari of such idle nature!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: ...Back to the topic. Though I did not elaborate on the Wenut in detail when we passed through here earlier, the catastrophe that caused it should be familiar to you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The one that happened five hundred years ago...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Indeed. The Wenut must've been frozen in an instant. As it has been crystallized, its form remains in perpetuity.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: It's as if it would start burrowing through the earth again once unsealed.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This moment will be frozen in time...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aghh! Paimon doesn't want to end up like that!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You say what happened to the Wenut happened in an instant... Ah! No! No! Just thinking of it scares Paimon!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I won't let that happen!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Y—Yeah! Paimon won't let something so horrible happen to {NICKNAME} either.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hmph. Then you should thank us Pari.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: During those days of ruin, many species and races, including the Pari, gave their lives... Sometimes, even things more precious than their lives.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Their sacrifices are why we are spared from facing the same irrevocable fate.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: And just so. As I was not there to witness the catastrophe, when this land faces danger once again, I must take action...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then, from what you're saying, this Wenut is even older than you are, which should also make it your elder.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: However, it will not be returning to life. It has been sealed in its crystallized state for centuries. Perhaps the only fate that awaits it is gradual dissolution.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: With how severe the loss of life was during the catastrophe, the Wenut, like countless other unfortunate souls, were frozen at the moment that calamity struck.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: But many more suffered even graver fates than this poor fool before us, for they had already worn away beneath the grinding passing of time itself.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: To this day, nothing remains of them. Not memory nor memorial.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: This one before us only lingers because of its immense size, and the fact that it has been hidden away in this cave from the glaring eye of the sun and lashing winds. Thus, the intactness of its condition.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: However, no being on this land can overcome time. Not even remains and husks will endure. One day, there will be nothing left of it, either.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That sounds kinda sad... Not having any trace that shows you lived once...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hm. The records left here by the humans should have something relating to the Wenut. I presume such a thing is rare for humans, no?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: From what I heard my elder say, aside from the Order of Skeptics, there were also researchers from the forest here seeking inquiry.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Though some humans believe that the Setekh Wenut is the completed state of a Quicksand Eel... To hold such theories and assumptions makes one worry for the contents recorded by these humans.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That information's not reliable at all!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Think! These records are obviously false, yet you still enthusiastically found a human to serve as your "Yasnapati"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe before this crystal is entirely corroded, the poems and odes dedicated to you will have changed beyond our recognition.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe the Bloomguard mentioned in the odes might not be pink or cute, but instead have a rough but reliable exterior, a mild and respectful personality, and act with rationality and calmness... Hmm?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That sounds a lot like the idealized image of a guardian.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But that sounds nothing like you, Sorush.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Absolutely not! Wait, I believe I understand what my elder desires. She must be reminding me to find a better way to record my deeds...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hm. My elder does possess foresight indeed. I must offer her my deepest thanks.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't think she meant that...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sorush brought us through here while bringing us to see Zurvan, remember?
